failure_caught: A font wiring regression that pointed bold, italic or bold-italic at a family without the dashboard status glyphs (or that dropped the symbols fallback) would render the spinner, check and arrow glyphs as replacement boxes in the GUI terminal.
criticality_reason: The failure is limited to the appearance of status indicator glyphs in the GUI; no state, routing or ownership depends on them, so the consequence is cosmetic (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:49-57).
signal_reason: The accepted symbol set changes with the developer's ~/Library/Fonts: without the nerd font install_terminal_fonts returns current_monospace where all four FontIds are the same monospace id (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:34-48, 108-110), so the style mapping is unasserted and only one braille glyph is checked; it also relies on Fonts::has_glyphs, the API paint_terminal explicitly distrusts (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:1052-1060).
uniqueness_reason: No other test exercises install_terminal_fonts' family selection (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:98-156): the paint tests at src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:196-260 and src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:388-427 cover glyph output, never which family each style is bound to.
fidelity_reason: The production install path (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:98-156) and a real egui Context are used, but the assertion stops at atlas coverage (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:158-186) rather than painting a cell, so the claim 'renders the glyphs' is only partially exercised.
recommendation_reason: S=1: on a machine without the nerd fonts the test degenerates to one braille glyph and the style mapping is vacuous, while the behaviour it claims still needs protection - assert per-style family identity from a fixture font directory and paint one status cell instead of querying has_glyphs.

behavior: paint_terminal paints CJK and emoji cells missing from the outline font through the CoreText fallback as exactly two image meshes, each inside its wide cell, keeping the terminal red for the CJK glyph and the emoji's own colours; it does this both with the nerd fonts installed and with plain monospace.
failure_caught: A fallback that stops producing native artwork (replacement galleys instead), draws at the wrong column, stretches a glyph into one cell, or drops the cell foreground turns 界 and 🙂 into white boxes or misplaced glyphs, making non-Latin terminal output unreadable in the GUI.
criticality_reason: Reading CJK or emoji output is a real workflow, but only non-ASCII content is affected and the same session can be read in the TUI, so this is a bounded feature failure (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:1051-1092).
signal_reason: The assertions are decisive: exactly two meshes, per-column bounds with a one-pixel tolerance, the clip rect, non-empty texture pixels, red foreground for 界 and a colour gradient for 🙂 (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:224-259), so a mesh-free fallback, a one-cell draw or a monochrome emoji is rejected.
uniqueness_reason: Only src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:196-260 checks what the native fallback paints; the cache tests at src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:264-302 and src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:306-385 count rasterizations, and the icon test at src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:388-427 checks shape ordering, so glyph placement and colour fidelity are protected here alone.
fidelity_reason: It runs the production paint_terminal and rasterize with real CoreText and real egui texture upload, i.e. the full OS text-rendering boundary the claim is about (src/bin/ovrcr-gui/native_glyph.rs:281-355).
recommendation_reason: Precise, high-fidelity protection of the native fallback's placement and colour, with no equivalent coverage; keep.

behavior: Painting a 40x30 screen of 600 distinct CJK glyphs rasterizes exactly 600 glyphs on the first frame, and a second paint of the same screen reuses the cache with zero further rasterizations.
failure_caught: A cache that misses on repeated frames (a per-paint map, or a key that includes the cell or rect) would run 600 CoreText rasterizations and texture uploads every frame for a CJK or emoji screen, collapsing the GUI's frame rate on exactly the content this fallback exists for.
criticality_reason: The consequence is GUI performance on non-ASCII screens, recoverable by using the TUI; it does not corrupt state, so it stays below the major-workflow band (src/bin/ovrcr-gui/native_glyph.rs:147-160).
signal_reason: It is a complete invariant for the cache-hit claim: exactly 600 rasters on frame one and an unchanged count on frame two (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:283-301), so any per-frame re-rasterization or missed reuse is caught.
uniqueness_reason: Distinct from the eviction test at src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:306-385: this one (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:264-302) proves hit reuse at the production cap, while the eviction test proves the sweep with a lowered cap; no other suite touches NativeGlyphs (src/bin/ovrcr-gui/native_glyph.rs:129-225).
fidelity_reason: paint_terminal and NativeGlyphs::paint run for real against CoreText; the only test instrument is the cfg(test) rasterize_calls counter, which observes rather than replaces the behaviour (src/bin/ovrcr-gui/native_glyph.rs:129-135, 190-193).
recommendation_reason: Decisive invariant for a real GUI performance failure mode with no other protection; keep.
cost_drivers: 0.450s one hosted attempt; rasterizes 600 distinct CJK glyphs through CoreText in one paint, twice painted

behavior: With the entry cap lowered to 4, four frames over two sets of six glyphs show that frame two keeps set A cached (12 entries), frame three sweeps A down to B's six entries without a re-raster, and frame four rasterizes A again - i.e. the sweep retains entries stamped in the previous frame only.
failure_caught: A sweep that evicted entries in the frame they were used, or no sweep at all, would either re-rasterize every glyph on every frame or grow the cache and its GPU textures without bound over a long session, ending in a stall or memory exhaustion.
criticality_reason: Unbounded texture growth degrades and eventually crashes the GUI process, but sessions live in the server and the user can restart the window, so this is a bounded failure (src/bin/ovrcr-gui/native_glyph.rs:124-134).
signal_reason: The four-frame assertion sequence separates all three plausible defects - no sweep (len stays 12), a too-aggressive sweep (frame three re-rasters B), and a sweep that does nothing until the cap is exceeded - with counts and lengths after each frame (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:340-384).
uniqueness_reason: Only src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:306-385 asserts the sweep; the other cache test at src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:264-302 proves hit reuse at the production cap, so the retention rule (src/bin/ovrcr-gui/native_glyph.rs:166-173) has no other protection.
fidelity_reason: The sweep logic is the production one, but the test-only with_max_entries(4) substitutes the threshold, so the production 4096 cap and a real screen's churn are not exercised (src/bin/ovrcr-gui/native_glyph.rs:147-162).
recommendation_reason: The only test of the eviction rule, with a decisive frame-by-frame signal; the lowered cap is a scale limit, not redundancy.
cost_drivers: 0.139s one hosted attempt; four paints against a lowered four-entry cache cap

behavior: App::show only records closing = true when the viewport reports a close request and never stops the PTY inside the egui pass; App::close, called from on_exit, stops the dashboard and then the demo root.
failure_caught: Stopping the Terminal inside show() would join the PTY reader while the egui context lock is held; the reader's Context::request_repaint then blocks until epaint's 10s deadlock panic, so every window close would freeze or panic and could leave the dashboard child running.
criticality_reason: A close that blocks the frame or panics is a major workflow failure of the GUI itself (the user force-quits and the dashboard child may survive), though it does not lose server-side sessions (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:453-468).
signal_reason: It asserts the elapsed frame time, that the Terminal is still present, that closing was recorded, that no error surfaced, and that app.close() then removes the demo root (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:674-689), which separates the deadlock from a correct deferral.
uniqueness_reason: This is the only test of the close and on_exit path: tests/gui.rs:385-422 exercises Demo cleanup but never App::show's close handling (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:453-468), so the lock-ordering defect has no other protection.
fidelity_reason: It runs the real App::show inside a real egui Context with a real spawned dashboard on a PTY and a real temp root (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:637-660), i.e. the full lifecycle boundary.
recommendation_reason: The only protection for a close-path deadlock in the GUI host; high-signal and high-fidelity, keep.
cost_drivers: 6.576s one hosted attempt; spawns a real ovrcr demo dashboard on a PTY, waits for it to become ready, then runs one closed-viewport egui frame

behavior: App::show consumes Cmd-K before the terminal widget, requests terminal focus whenever the palette opens or no widget holds focus, keeps the pending intent across startup offers and dashboard restarts, and injects the dashboard palette sequence only on an alternate-screen dashboard that shows OVRCR.
failure_caught: If Cmd-K were handled only while the terminal already had focus, or focus stayed on another control, the GUI's command palette could not be opened whenever another widget had focus and the key would leak to that widget or be typed into the terminal instead.
criticality_reason: Losing the host shortcut degrades one navigation affordance with a workaround (the dashboard's own palette keys and the TUI), so it is a bounded feature failure (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:453-470).
signal_reason: It asserts that focus left the competing control, that the key event was consumed, that the palette appears within five seconds after both a live and a stopped dashboard, and that it survives the Command release (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:784-900); the palette check is a substring wait, so it cannot tell which palette state opened.
uniqueness_reason: tests/gui.rs:282-384 drives the Dashboard palette API and tests/gui.rs:258-281 checks the key encoder, so the egui host focus and global-shortcut failure mode (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:453-470, src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:500-520) is only covered here.
fidelity_reason: It runs real egui frames against a real App with a real dashboard process and PTY, including the actual event plumbing that decides focus and key consumption (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:697-720).
recommendation_reason: Distinct integration boundary (host window focus and key routing) with real processes; keep.
cost_drivers: 7.372s one hosted attempt; spawns a real dashboard on a PTY, drives a live and a restarted dashboard, and polls the screen for up to 5s in each variant

behavior: waiting_startup_decision returns the offer title only when the screen shows an 'OVRCR · startup' prompt whose last line is one of the known answer forms, returns None when the offer is answered or not yet drawn, and errors on an unknown title so the harness never answers an offer it does not recognise.
failure_caught: A laxer parser that matched the answer line without the known title set would let the GUI tests auto-decline a new offer such as 'Restart OVRCR server - all running sessions will stop', silently changing the state under test; a stricter one would never decline and the GUI tests would time out.
criticality_reason: The subject is test-harness code, so a regression can only mislead or stall the GUI suites; no product path changes, which is a maintenance consequence (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:928-960).
signal_reason: Four cases cover both branches: two recognised offers, an answered and an undrawn screen returning None, and an unknown title returning an error (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:963-982); the alternate-screen early return in decline_test_startup_prompt (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:909-916) and the send path are untested.
uniqueness_reason: The product-side offer vocabulary is covered by tests/client_startup.rs and the GUI acceptance tests at src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:693-906 fail if this helper stops recognising offers; only the strictness assertion (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:944-956) is extra here.
fidelity_reason: The subject (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:928-960) is a #[cfg(test)]-only helper fed three hand-written screen strings at src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:963-982; no live vt100 screen is read and the sending half of the harness (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:908-925) is not exercised.
recommendation_reason: It guards the harness that the two GUI acceptance tests depend on; the pragmatic call is keep rather than improve, because the product behaviour it mirrors is covered by the client_startup suite and the harness fails loudly (timeout) if recognition breaks.

behavior: rasterize renders 界 and 🙂 through CoreText at scale 1 and 2 so the image doubles when DPI doubles, uses the bold-italic Menlo face for styled text, and applies the colour's alpha to the CGContext so a dimmed colour keeps partial opacity.
failure_caught: Rasterizing at point size instead of the pixel scale blurs every retina glyph; ignoring bold/italic in the CTFont name makes styled characters render regular; dropping CGContextSetAlpha makes dim cells full brightness and loses the dimmed-state cue.
criticality_reason: The consequences are visual - blur, lost style, lost dimming - with no state or control effect, so this is a cosmetic contract (src/bin/ovrcr-gui/native_glyph.rs:281-300).
signal_reason: Size doubling is checked per dimension with a one-pixel tolerance, styled pixels must differ, dim alpha must land in (0,128], and a null CF value must map to None (src/bin/ovrcr-gui/native_glyph.rs:233-279); a bold/italic swap still passes because only 'differs' is asserted.
uniqueness_reason: Distinct from the paint test at src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:196-260: this one (src/bin/ovrcr-gui/native_glyph.rs:233-279) pins DPI scale, font traits and alpha inside rasterize, which the mesh and colour assertions cannot see.
fidelity_reason: rasterize is called directly against real CoreText and CoreGraphics, so the platform boundary the claim is about is fully exercised (src/bin/ovrcr-gui/native_glyph.rs:281-355).
recommendation_reason: Direct, precise coverage of the rasterizer's three stated properties with real OS frameworks; keep.
cost_drivers: 0.343s one hosted attempt; six CoreText rasterizations at two pixel scales

behavior: dashboard_service_with returns the installed launchd or systemd definition only when its ProgramArguments or ExecStart is the intended executable and the OVRCR_SOCKET assignment appears exactly once; it refuses a duplicated definition, a different executable, and a listener whose peer pid is not the loaded manager's MainPID.
failure_caught: Without the peer-pid and manager check the Dashboard would take over - shut down and replace - a socket served by an unmanaged or foreign OVRCR process, killing sessions it does not own; without the executable check it would adopt a definition another install pointed at a different binary.
criticality_reason: Taking over a listener it does not own destroys another instance's running sessions - wrong ownership and a threat to durable session state (src/service.rs:280-290).
signal_reason: Four assertions cover the definition echo, the duplicate-assignment refusal, the executable mismatch text and the peer-pid mismatch (src/service.rs:890-941), and the manager stub returns the exact launchctl and systemctl output formats; the socket-path mismatch branch (src/service.rs:240-243) and the O_NOFOLLOW symlink refusal are untested.
uniqueness_reason: tests/service.rs:264-280 covers the install path's refusal through managed_connection (src/service.rs:629-640); the Dashboard startup variant, its executable match and its duplicate-assignment rule are asserted only here.
fidelity_reason: Real definition files, a real Unix socket pair whose kernel peer credentials are read through src/client.rs:406-415, and real ServiceConfig resolution are used; only the launchctl/systemctl process is a stub script, which is the external boundary tests cannot own.
recommendation_reason: The only direct coverage of the Dashboard's service ownership guard, whose regression kills another instance's sessions; keep.
cost_drivers: 0.052s one hosted attempt; a real Unix listener and stream pair per platform plus a stub manager script executed for print/show and is-active
